description: Storm Surge Inundation and Hurricane Strike Frequency Map is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by EPA, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency; NOAA, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration; FEMA, Federal Emergency Management Agency. Storm surge (the abnormal rise of water generated by a storm, over and above the predicted astronomical tides) can lead to saltwater flooding of locations far inland from the coast. This map can help identify which neighborhoods are vulnerable to such flooding when hurricanes, tropical storms, or nor'easters arrive. Use the tool to view maps showing. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Flooding – Coastal, High Winds. Assets: Natural Areas and Wildlife, Property, Transportation and Mobility. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
